_comment: House rules for the four-player game, drawn from the variants listed at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/500_(card_game). Data only: labels and defaults live here so the picker on the home page and the validator in server/gameOptions.js can never disagree about what an option is called or what it defaults to. The two-player game predates this and keeps its own settings.

options.label: Name for the no-tricks bid
options.help: Some tables call it Nullo. Naming only — the contract plays the same either way.

options.label: Misère biddable at any time
options.help: Standard play only lets Misère in once someone has bid at the seven level. Turn this on for unrestricted bidding.

options.label: You may bid again after passing
options.help: Standard play puts you out of the auction for good once you pass.

options.label: Split the colours
options.help: The special contracts outbid the black suits at their level but not the red ones: Misère beats 7♠ and 7♣ but not 7♦ or 7♥, Open Misère beats 8♠/8♣, Hi-Lo beats 9♠/9♣, Double Nullo beats 10♠/10♣.

options.label: Play the hand if everyone passes
options.help: Instead of redealing, the hand is played at no trumps with nobody on a contract and every trick worth ten to whoever takes it.

options.label: Open Misère
options.help: Worth 500. Your hand goes face up after the first trick.

options.label: Blind Misère
options.help: Worth 1000, and only as your first call of the auction — properly it's bid before you look at your hand, so it runs on trust here.

options.label: Hi-Lo (Even Stevens)
options.help: Worth 350. Win exactly five tricks — no more, no fewer. Your partner folds.

options.label: Double Nullo (Grand Nullo)
options.help: Worth 500. Both partners play, and neither may win a trick.

options.label: Joker may be led at no trumps
options.help: In a no-trump or Misère contract, leading the Joker and nominating a suit is allowed even when you could follow. Turn this off and the Joker can only be thrown when you're void.

options.label: J5 — jacks high at no trumps
options.help: In a no-trump contract each jack outranks the ace of its own suit.

options.label: Ten points a trick for the defenders
options.help: Turn this off and only a won contract scores anything.

options.label: Slam bonus
options.help: Take all ten tricks on a contract worth less than 250 and score 250 instead.

options.label: Must bid to win
options.help: Passing 500 on trick points alone isn't enough — the winning hand has to be a made contract.

options.label: Out the back door at −500
options.help: A team down to −500 or worse loses the game there and then.

options.label: Point spread ends the game
options.help: Once one team is negative and the gap between the teams reaches 500, the team in front wins.

options.label: Ralphing
options.help: Go down by more than three tricks and you're barred from bidding on the next hand. Your partner still may.
